newsitem.title: MEXICO: Venezuelan leader calls for calm in Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan leader calls for calm in Ecuador.

text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera called on Friday for "good sense" to prevail in Ecuador, which is gripped by a state of emergency and unrest on the streets after a congressional vote to fire the president.
"All we Americans, Hispanic Americans, above all Latin Americans, hope good sense will prevail in the country," Caldera told reporters during an official visit to Mexico.
Ecuador's Congress voted on Thursday night to sack President Abdala Bucaram and named a replacement but Bucaram refused to accept the decision.
Ecuadoreans woke up on Friday with three presidents after Vice President Rosalia Arteaga also claimed she was the country's rightful leader.
Caldera said the crisis in Ecuador was "very worrying" and said he wanted "everything to be resolved in a harmonious and peaceful way" but avoided going into details.
The Venezuelan leader later ducked questions on Ecuador at a news conference to wind up his trip, saying he wanted to avoid "meddling without sufficient knowledge in an internal matter of Ecuador's".
